rationale: This is a mechanical equal-weight rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals (Idle-Asset Value Trap and Short-Term Funding Sales Trap) whose legs share a common price-scaled cheapness component, so it is an ensemble rather than a new mechanism and will almost surely land between the two parent results.

Pairing the archive's strongest value leg with a genuinely untested standalone current-asset productivity trend is defensible and avoids sign-inversion from multiplying a signed quality term, but the 50/50 rank weighting hands half the signal to a leg with no standalone evidence and risks diluting the parent's alpha.

Combining maintenance-cash-supported sales value with an independently ranked (rather than multiplied) easing-funding-pressure leg is a coherent construction and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it is close in spirit to the previous proposal and its incremental information over the archived parent is likely modest.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value, differing only by replacing lt with lct in the denominator of the EBITDA-productivity trend, which is exactly the kind of superficial substitution the objective warns against.

Swapping the flow-based maintenance cash margin for the stock-based retained-earnings term in the archived Earned-Cash Discount is a modest but economically motivated change, and the stated sign logic (nonnegative cash yield leg, direction set by the quality term) correctly matches what the expression computes — though it remains a recombination of two well-worn archive components.

A direct rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content; blending a t_alpha 1.81 signal with a t_alpha 2.88 signal is portfolio bookkeeping, not a test of a distinct mechanism.
